title: Getting young minds into design ｜ 让年轻一代走近设计

sents.en: Recently, a leading design federation in the UK warned that the UK could face a creative skills shortage, after the latest figures revealed a drop of almost 10 percent in students studying Design and Technology.
sents.cn: 近日，英国一家顶尖设计联合会警告称，随着最新数据显示修读“设计与技术”的学生人数下降了近10%，英国可能面临创意技能人才短缺。

sents.en: These figures showed that the number of pupils that sat exams in Design and Technology fell 10 percent from 204,788 to 185,279 last year.
sents.cn: 数据显示，去年参加“设计与技术”考试的学生人数从204,788人降至185,279人，降幅达10%。

sents.en: Chief executive John Kampfner of the Creative Industries Federation thinks that this drop in figures has worrying implications for the skills pipeline in Britain·s hugely successful arts and creative industries.
sents.cn: 创意产业联合会的首席执行官约翰∙坎普夫纳认为，这一数字下降对英国极为成功的艺术与创意产业的“人才输送管道”而言是个令人担忧的信号。他说：“在动画制作、特效等许多岗位上，我们已经出现了技能短缺。

sents.en: He said, ·We already have skills shortages in many jobs such as animation and special effects.· He added: ·Engineering, which requires a similar mix of creative and technical skills, also has recruitment problems.·
sents.cn: ”他补充道：“工程行业同样面临招聘难题，因为它需要创意与技术能力的类似结合。”

sents.en: Many other designers and architects have expressed concern over the future supply of home-grown talent for UK firms, and industry bodies have pointed out that there has been a lack of roots-level support.
sents.cn: 许多其他设计师和建筑师也对英国企业未来本土人才的供给表示担忧，行业机构也指出，底层（基础性）支持一直不足。

sents.en: However, if these designers had visited the Design Museum shop in London earlier this year their fears may have been eased.
sents.cn: 不过，如果这些设计师今年早些时候去过伦敦的设计博物馆商店，他们的担忧或许会缓解。

sents.en: With £10 to spend, they could have bought a fascinating children·s toy called ·Dazzle Racer·.
sents.cn: 花10英镑，他们就能买到一个名为“炫光赛车手”的奇妙儿童玩具。

sents.en: An automotive cylinder, it included a wind-up, elastic-band-powered mechanism, minimal parts, all 100 percent recycled and lots of stickers.
sents.cn: 那是一个汽车圆柱体造型，内含上发条、橡皮筋驱动的机构，零件极少，全部采用100%可回收材料，还配有许多贴纸。

sents.en: It was good fun, simple, eye-catching and very original.
sents.cn: 它好玩、简单、吸睛，而且极具创意。

sents.en: Well you·d expect the Design Museum to commission and make some interesting items, but this one was different.
sents.cn: 你大概会想到设计博物馆委托制作一些有趣的物品，但这一件有所不同。

sents.en: Designed by a group of six Year 9 and Year 10 boys from Finchley Catholic High School, the toy was the winning entry in the museum·s 2015 Design Ventura competition, which brings the business of design to life for students aged 13 to 16 by challenging them to develop a new creative, sustainable and commercially feasible product for the Design Museum shop and attracts hundreds of entries nationwide.
sents.cn: 这款玩具由芬奇利天主教学校六名九年级和十年级男生设计，是博物馆2015年“设计文图拉”（DesignVentura）竞赛的夺冠作品。该竞赛面向13至16岁学生，要求他们为设计博物馆商店开发一款富有创意、可持续且具有商业可行性的新产品，让设计的商业逻辑鲜活地呈现在学生面前，并在全国吸引了数百件参赛作品。

sents.en: ·We did Design Ventura in my previous school,· says Liam Hourican, Finchley Catholic High School·s design technology curriculum leader.
sents.cn: “我在上一所学校时就带学生参加过设计文图拉，”芬奇利天主教学校的设计技术课程负责人利亚姆∙霍里根说，“四年前我换到这所学校后，就把这个项目带了过来，因为它能帮助学生培养诸多技能。

sents.en: ·Then when I changed schools four years ago, I introduced it here because it helps to develop so many skills.·
The theme for last year·s competition was ·Move·, and Hourican began with three groups working in lunch breaks and after school before selecting the group with the most innovative idea.
sents.cn: 去年竞赛的主题是“运动”（Move），霍里根最初组织了三个小组，利用午休和课余时间工作，再从中选出创意最出众的小组。

sents.en: Each participating school may submit just one proposal.
sents.cn: 每所参赛学校只能提交一份方案。

sents.en: ·It·s the taking part and doing the work which is important,· he says.
sents.cn: “重要的是参与和付出，”他说，“我从没想过我们会赢。

sents.en: ·And I never dreamt we·d win.·

Catherine Ritman Smith, head of learning at the Design Museum, is expecting around 10,000 participants aged 13 to 16 to take part this year and says that the project · funded by Deutsche Bank as part of its youth engagement programme Born To Be · is the biggest event in the museum·s calendar.
sents.cn: 设计博物馆的学习主管凯瑟琳∙里特曼∙史密斯预计，今年将有约一万名13至16岁的青少年参与。她说，这一项目由德意志银行通过其青少年参与计划“生而为之”（BornToBe）资助，是博物馆年度日程中规模最大的活动。

sents.en: ·We started Design Ventura with around 800 young people in 2010 and it has grown steadily since,· she says.
sents.cn: “2010年我们启动设计文图拉时只有约800名年轻人，此后稳步增长，”她说。

sents.en: ·Teachers like it because the skills are all transferable and it helps to validate the value of design as a subject,· she explains, telling me that nearly 600 schools have taken part so far.
sents.cn: “教师喜欢它，因为这些技能都具有可迁移性，也有助于证明设计作为一门学科的价值，”她解释道，并告诉我迄今已有近600所学校参与。

sents.en: So how does the competition work?
sents.cn: 那么竞赛是如何运作的呢？

sents.en: A single-word theme is announced in the summer.
sents.cn: 每年夏天会公布一个单词的主题。

sents.en: This year it is ·Change·.
sents.cn: 今年的主题是“改变”（Change）。

sents.en: Schools work with groups to produce imaginative design ideas for a product in simple materials that could sell for £10 in the Design Museum Shop.
sents.cn: 各校以小组形式，用简易材料为设计博物馆商店构思一款售价10英镑的、富有想象力的产品设计。

sents.en: Participating schools then register by November and eventually submit their design idea.
sents.cn: 参赛学校于11月前完成注册，并最终提交设计方案。

sents.en: Along the way there is training and support for teachers and tutoring for students from designers.
sents.cn: 在此过程中，教师会获得培训与支持，学生也会得到设计师的辅导。

sents.en: An additional bonus is when the winners see their design on sale in the spring of the following year.
sents.cn: 额外的惊喜是：获奖者能在次年春天看到自己的设计被摆上货架出售。

sents.en: Hourican and his pupils have happy memories of spending a whole day at the museum, having been selected as one of 10 shortlisted schools to present their idea to a panel of judges, including designer Jasper Conran.
sents.cn: 霍里根和学生们至今仍愉快地记得，他们作为入围的10所学校之一，在博物馆度过了一整天，向包括设计师贾斯珀∙康兰在内的评委团展示创意。

sents.en: Then they worked with the Kin Design Studio in Shoreditch, met designers at their school and attended a lunch with Deutsche Bank employees.
sents.cn: 随后，他们与肖尔迪奇的Kin设计工作室合作，在校内会见设计师，并参加了与德意志银行员工的午餐会。

sents.en: The students helped to make decisions and there were plenty of discussions · they changed the product·s name, for example.
sents.cn: 学生们参与决策，进行了大量讨论——比如，他们改了产品的名字。

sents.en: ·One of the really useful things about this competition,· says Hourican, ·is that there·s a commercial element because the product is going on sale for real and the boys had to learn about budgeting and marketing, as well as designing their game.· Profits go to charity.
sents.cn: “这项竞赛真正有用的一点，”霍里根说，“在于它的商业元素——产品真的会上市销售，男生们必须学习预算和营销，以及游戏的设计。”利润用于慈善。“获胜团队可以自行选择利润的去向，”里特曼∙史密斯说，“芬奇利天主教学校的产品为大奥蒙德街儿童医院筹得约1000英镑。”往年的获奖作品包括一个名为“鸽子旗”的自制布料套装，以及一款可三折、如钱包大小、两端各设球门的旅行游戏“Badoiiing”。K)ItcoststheschoolsnothingtoparticipateinDesignVentura;theprofessionaldesignersprovidetheirservicesforfree.AmongthemarearchitectAsifKhan,aDesignMuseumtrusteewhohasworkedasdesigner-in-residenceatthemuseum,helpingemergingarchitects.HehasrecentlybeencommissionedtodesignthenewMuseumofLondonbuildinginSmithfield.K）学校参与设计文图拉无需任何费用；专业设计师免费提供服务。其中包括建筑师阿西夫∙汗，他是设计博物馆的受托人，曾担任馆内驻场设计师，助力新锐建筑师成长。他最近受委托设计位于史密斯菲尔德的新伦敦博物馆大楼。L)AnotheristelevisionpresenterandinteriordesignerNaomiCleaver,whoisoneofthecompetition·sjudges.·I'mverykeentoencourageyoungpeople,·shesays,observingthatdesignbringstogetherothersubjectssuchasliterature,art,history,geographyandscience.·Nowthatdesigneducationislimitedinthecurriculum,I·mallinfavourofcompetitionssuchasDesignVentura,whichhelpstobringthestandardcurriculumtolife,·saysCleaver.·Andthejudgingdayisterrificfun.Someofthesestudentsareveryimaginative.Onegrouppresentedtheirideaintheformofapuppetshowandweseesomemarvelousdemonstrationmodels.·I·malwaysimpressedbythelevelsofconfidenceandthesupportthestudentsgetfromtheirteachers.·L）另一位是电视主持人兼室内设计师娜奥米∙克利弗，她也是竞赛评委之一。“我非常乐意鼓励年轻人，”她说，并指出设计能将文学、艺术、历史、地理和科学等其他学科融会贯通。“如今设计教育在课程中受到限制，我大力支持诸如设计文图拉这样的竞赛，它让标准课程鲜活起来，”克利弗说。“评审日也充满乐趣。
